### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**13** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a83c366702b26d653a975d533dde4dabb30030e1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ef1fd06e9b0f8e4b98997b50758b3874068f70a5` — the merge of head `616dbbda179dbafe42143eb1f748e9a85a91c94f` into base `a83c366702b26d653a975d533dde4dabb30030e1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ef1fd06e9b0f8e4b98997b50758b3874068f70a5 && git checkout ef1fd06e9b0f8e4b98997b50758b3874068f70a5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a83c366702b26d653a975d533dde4dabb30030e1 616dbbda179dbafe42143eb1f748e9a85a91c94f && git checkout -B drift-repro a83c366702b26d653a975d533dde4dabb30030e1 && git merge --no-ff 616dbbda179dbafe42143eb1f748e9a85a91c94f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a83c366702b26d653a975d533dde4dabb30030e1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c0b7cb13cb11498031bde97a8673982e7dbb58ac`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-state.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-flow-slot.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-flow-slot.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-declared-override-first-boot-pull.integration.test.ts, .changeset/32613-two-holder-override-slots.md (its declaration lines and level) + read as cited code, not reviewed: packages/metadata-protocol/src/served-override.ts, protocol-package-bindings.ts (`SEALED_ROW_SERVED_OVERRIDE_TYPES`), protocol-environment-rows.ts (`shippingPackageIds`, `soleShippingPackage`), protocol-artifact-lookup.ts, the two callers of `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` in protocol-meta-list-reads.ts and protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, `getArtifactItem` in packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3.

First round, read at 2026-11-13T16:12Z. Inputs: card #32613 with claim 6855902049 and report 6858019637, the PR body, the diff against merge base `2c98485d` (eight files), the knocks 6858065729 and 6858122699. Claim 6858311083.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right for what the PR names: the env-wide lists stop serving entries they served, and no export or accepted input widens. `incomingTakesStoredFlowSlot` changes its third parameter, but the package entry does not export it (only `shadowedStoredRowsOf`), so no published signature moves.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing an author can write is added, refused or given a new meaning. A declared override always meant "serve this in place of the package's item"; the runtime now honours it for the second holder too.
- The declared scope is narrower than the code in two places (M1, S1).

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` follows from `none`. The `!` title and the BREAKING banner are kept, as a `(narrowing)` arm requires.
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is admitted for the kind `none`, and the reason given holds: no key and no stored shape moves.
- M1 and S1 change what the BREAKING line must name, not the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs are not read for this verdict: a FAIL does not wait on them.
- File surface: inside claim 6855902049 (the four `metadata-protocol` files and tests).
- `Fixes #32613` closes the card. The census twin #32859 is carried by the report.
- Order, from the PR: after #32741 (merged), before #32552 (PR #33129, knocked to this seat, not read yet); #32820 shares `protocol-registry-hydration.ts` and runs after.
- `main` is four commits past the merge base, none on a path of this diff.
- The PR lists `os-elon-musk` as requested reviewer, which is the seat's own account. The seat's.
- The ablation readings are the report's and were not run here.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-flow-slot.ts`, `protocol-registry-hydration.ts` (the boot pull). Holds. A row is an override when it declares the override of any package that ships the name, each judged through its own pair by the one predicate. With two holders' overrides the later one takes the bare slot and carries the other, and a package-less row read after either is carried and never takes the slot. The slot is transport only, as the docblock now says. The unit pins hold both orders, the FROM case and a pair that declares a non-shipper; the integration pins read what the first pull armed. The single-shipper path is the same code with a set of one.

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` (the lists). The rewrite keeps the three old outcomes: no shipper and a bound shipper keep the item, one shipper narrows as before (`soleShippingPackage` was already "exactly one id"). The new branch drops, under two or more shippers, an item bound to a pair whose body declares a shipper's override. It is judged on the item's binding and body, never on a stamp. Right for the case the card names; see S1 for its reach.

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-state.ts` (`declinesStoredRow`). The flow branch is the same judgment moved into a helper; the added guard for a missing row answers as before. The last branch is where the diff does more than it says (M1).

Findings:

- **M1 must-fix. The every-shipper judgment also moves six sealed types, unnamed and unpinned.** Derived from the code, not run. The last return of `declinesStoredRow` reads `(servesSealedOverrideRow(type) || action) && servedOverrideOfAShipper(type, name)`. On `main` both arms judged the row against `packagedArtifactOwner` alone; this diff moves both arms to every shipper. `servesSealedOverrideRow` is `page`, `app`, `dataset`, `doc`, `book` and `mapping`. So for those six, the second holder's declared override goes FROM declined (its shipped item served) TO served, at its own address and wherever the reads ask this gate. The docblock, the PR table, the changeset and the BREAKING line say `action`; the new pins cover flow and action. `dataset` and `mapping` are held per namespace since #31700, so two holders are reachable today, and a mapping's by-name read is the one the import door resolves through. For `page`, `app`, `doc` and `book`, where two packages ship one name, what a read naming no package answers once two overrides are served is not shown. The direction is ADR-0150 D4's own. Owed, one of: keep the every-shipper judgment to `action` here and file the six; or keep it, pin one sealed type in both registration orders (each address, the lists, the read naming no package) and name the six in the FROM → TO table and the changeset.
- **S1 should-fix. The list filter moves every type, and the declaration names two.** The new branch runs for every `request.type` but `package`. The `Clause-②:` line is worded for "a name", but the title, the BREAKING line (`GET /meta/flow`, `GET /meta/action`) and the table say flow and action. By the same code the pair's entry leaves the env-wide list of any type that serves a declared override under a name two packages ship (a dashboard, a report, an email template). Whether `main` listed that entry for those types is not measured here. Say which types move, with one pin on an overlay type, or scope the branch to the two the card names.
- **S2 should-fix. For an action, the pins stop at the protocol's reads.** The card asks the sweep to cover "the other execution-face readers" for flow and action. The flow's boot pull is pinned. For an action the pins read the two lists, the by-name read, the layered read and the served-overrides list. The hydrator still registers an action's override row under the bare name, wearing the envelope `lookupArtifactItem` answers for the pair's id; a pair ships no artifact, so `getArtifactItem` falls to the first composite of the name, the first shipper's. This diff does not touch that and `main` does the same, so it is no regression. But what a registry reader gets for each holder, in each order, is neither pinned nor named as carried. Pin it, or carry it by name to the card that follows on this face.
- **n1 nit.** The mixed case is not pinned: two shippers, one with a declared override and one without. The filter and the gate both reach it.

M1 is the ground of this verdict. The delta on the next head is this seat's.

Claim 6860332620. Everything the earlier record judged and the interdiff does not touch stands as read there: the boot-pull files of the Scope line are unchanged since `c0b7cb13`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand as judged in the earlier record.
- The declaration and the code now name the same two types. `flow` and `action` move; the changeset, the PR table and the BREAKING line say so, and the code moves nothing else (M1, S1 below).
- The mixed case (one holder overridden) is not claimed: the title and the changeset speak of a name where each package has its declared override.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, the `!` title, the BREAKING banner and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: unchanged, and right as before.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head, all concluded: 55 runs, 37 success, 18 skipped, none failed. The eight `Test Core` shards and `Check Changeset` are green.
- `main` is nine commits past the merge base `2c98485d`, none on a path of this diff.
- `Fixes #32613` and the mixed case. The card's expected answer (both overridden, both orders, flow and action, a one-holder CONTROL) is met. Its first fix-shape bullet (a bound override row is "never taken by the bare slot when two packages hold the name", flow and action) is not met for an action when only the second-registered holder is overridden: the first holder's slot on the served list and the execution view then carries the second holder's override. By the report's reading with the owner-only judgment put back, that is `main`'s answer too, and this diff does not make it; it is recorded on #33131 (6858574856). The card also says #32552 waits on it because an action "shows the same wrong entry (`alpha:OVERRIDE-beta` when alpha registers first)", which is the shape that pin still measures. Whether the card closes here or reads `Part of`, and whether #33129 may land ahead of #33131's item 3, is the seat's.
- #33131's triage note (6858501842) says item 3 "matches `main`" and carries no defect yet. The measured case was written three minutes after it: the execution view, which the engine arms from, lists one package's action slot with another package's override. A re-grade is the seat's to ask for; this seat does not grade.
- PR #33129 (PASS 6859128505, head `c35a911b`, unchanged). Its s1 named this branch: M1 was closed by leaving the six sealed types on the first-holder judgment, so its census, which leaves out a row that is the declared override of any shipper for every type, would stop naming a second holder's override of those six while the reads still decline it. Owed there before it lands: the census judges every shipper for `flow` and `action` only, or waits for #33131's item 1.
- The ablation readings, the mixed-case reading on `main` and the local runs are the report's; none was run here.
- The PR lists `os-elon-musk` as requested reviewer, the seat's own account. The seat's, as before.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-state.ts` (M1). Fixed, by the first of the two options. `action` takes its own return and is judged against every shipper through `servedOverrideOfAShipper`; the six sealed types return on the expression `main` has, `isServedOverrideRowOf(row, this.packagedArtifactOwner(…), installed)`, so nothing moves for them. The changeset says so and carries them to #33131 (item 1).

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` (S1). Fixed. Under two or more shippers the pair-slot drop runs for `flow` and `action` (`TWO_HOLDER_PAIR_SLOT_TYPES`, read through the plural map); any other type keeps the item, which is `main`'s answer in that branch. Carried to #33131 (item 2).

`packages/objectql/src/protocol-flow-custom-override.test.ts` (n1). The mixed case is pinned in both orders with either holder overridden. For a flow the lists and both addresses are exact. For an action the pin holds the overridden holder's own slot and address and says in its comment what it leaves out.

S2. Carried by name: the PR body, the changeset and #33131's item 3 name the action's registry face, with the measured case.

Findings:

- **n1 nit.** The changeset's carry sentence calls the residual "what a registry reader gets for each holder of an action name". The mixed pin shows it on the protocol's own served list and execution view (the first holder's slot, when only the second holder is overridden). The PR body says so; the changeset is what a release reader gets, and one sentence there would say the same.
- **n2 nit.** The action half of the mixed pin leaves the other holder's slot unpinned in both sub-cases. By the pin's own comment the leak needs the second-registered holder to be the overridden one, so with the first-registered holder overridden the lists could be pinned exactly, as the flow's are.

No must-fix. M1, S1 and n1 of record 6858448985 are closed on this head; S2 is carried by name.
